definition.name: Variable-frequency drive
definition.description: A drive accepts three-phase power and a run request, providing an abstracted variable-frequency motor output.

terminals.label: L1
terminals.purpose: First phase of the three-phase supply.

terminals.label: PE
terminals.purpose: Protective connection to the represented exposed conductive parts or protective network. It carries no intended normal load return and remains independent of switching the active conductors.

terminals.label: U
terminals.purpose: U variable-frequency motor output of the fundamental three-phase RMS abstraction. Measure between output phases or across the connected winding. It is separate from L1/L2/L3; PWM pulses and motor torque are excluded.

terminals.label: V
terminals.purpose: V variable-frequency motor output of the fundamental three-phase RMS abstraction. Measure between output phases or across the connected winding. It is separate from L1/L2/L3; PWM pulses and motor torque are excluded.

terminals.label: W
terminals.purpose: W variable-frequency motor output of the fundamental three-phase RMS abstraction. Measure between output phases or across the connected winding. It is separate from L1/L2/L3; PWM pulses and motor torque are excluded.

terminals.label: COM
terminals.purpose: Return reference for the internally biased conceptual 24 V RUN loop. A dry contact between RUN and COM requests operation. It is not mains neutral or protective earth.

terminals.label: RUN
terminals.purpose: Internally biased conceptual RUN input. Closing the actual dry-contact path to COM requests output; opening it removes that request. Real drive input polarity and parameter assignments depend on its manufacturer.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The enclosure supports and separates functional parts. This original teaching model is representative equipment, not a manufacturer drawing.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: The cover limits access to internal connections. Opening it here is a virtual inspection operation.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: Metal clamps establish connections to individual conductors. The circuit engine connects terminal IDs, not the apparent proximity of 3D wires.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: Mounting hardware supports the equipment. Screws, rail clips and glands are modelled separately from electrical connections.

parts.name: Electronic control board
parts.purpose: This conceptual board represents an electronic interface. The model follows stated input, output and power limits rather than reconstructing proprietary firmware.

parts.name: Display and indicators
parts.purpose: The display reports the model operating state. Meter readings come from the connected circuit, not a pre-recorded picture.

definition.abstraction: PWM waveforms and motor torque are not simulated. Output measurements describe the fundamental RMS abstraction.
